The Danish wind turbine manufacturer reported earnings before interest, taxes and special items of €483 million ($538 million), falling short of analysts' expectations. The results marked a reversal from the second quarter, when stronger-than-expected profitability prompted the company to raise its annual outlook.

The earnings miss raises questions for investors about the durability of Vestas' profitability improvements after several years of supply-chain disruptions and rising costs. The latest setback also highlights the financial risks associated with large offshore wind projects.

Vestas attributed the additional expenses to a broken turbine blade at the He Dreiht project in the German North Sea. Chief Financial Officer Jakob Wegge Larsen indicated that the financial impact would be limited to the third quarter.
The company narrowed its full-year operating profit margin forecast to 7.5% to 8.5%, compared with its previous range of 7% to 9%. Shares were down 7.6% in morning trading in Copenhagen.

title: Vestas shares tumble as German wind project costs weigh on quarterly profit
